findings.claim: `self_notMem_Ioi` duplicates an existing theorem in the same file: `notMem_Ioi_self` is already present later (`Order/Interval/Set/Basic.lean:576`). Adding a second name for the exact same statement grows the API unnecessarily and leaves two competing canonical names for the same fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not introduce `self_notMem_Ioi`; instead, deprecate the old `left_mem_Ioo` lemma to `notMem_Ioi_self` (or, if you want a renamed theorem, rename `notMem_Ioi_self` itself to the chosen canonical name and keep only a deprecated alias in the other direction).

findings.claim: `self_notMem_Iio` is also a duplicate: the file already has `notMem_Iio_self` later (`Order/Interval/Set/Basic.lean:580`). As above, this introduces two names for the same lemma without adding generality.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse `notMem_Iio_self` as the canonical endpoint-nonmembership lemma, or rename that existing theorem and keep a single deprecated alias rather than adding `self_notMem_Iio` as a fresh duplicate.

findings.claim: The rename/deprecation story is incomplete for the new `self_mem_Ici` / `self_mem_Iic` names. This file adds deprecated aliases from `left_mem_Ici` and `right_mem_Iic`, but unlike the surrounding interval API it does not also provide snake_case compatibility aliases for the new canonical names, so users following the usual `*_mem_*` migration pattern get an uneven API.
findings.suggested_fix: Add deprecated snake_case aliases for the new names, e.g. `alias self_mem_Ici := self_mem_Ici` is not possible directly, so introduce `@[deprecated (since := ...)] alias self_mem_Ici := self_mem_Ici`-style compatibility via appropriately named old-style aliases such as `self_mem_Ici`/`self_mem_Iic` snake_case forms (`self_mem_Ici` -> `self_mem_Ici` doesn't apply, but `self_mem_Ici` should get a `self_mem_Ici`-style old naming if your deprecation policy expects one), or document why these renamed lemmas intentionally do not participate in the usual camelCase/snake_case alias scheme.

findings.claim: This extends the `sub` API only on the left: you add `sub_right_injective_of_ne_top` and `sub_right_inj_of_ne_top`, but there is no matching `sub_right_strictMono_of_ne_top` nor the corresponding `sub_lt_sub_iff_right_of_ne_top` / `sub_le_sub_iff_right_of_ne_top`. That asymmetry makes the new monotonicity/comparison family feel incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the right-handed monotonicity/comparison lemmas for subtraction as companions to lines 205–214, or explicitly trim the new right-handed injectivity lemmas if the intended API is left-handed only.

findings.claim: `norm_deriv_le_one_of_mapsTo_ball` and `dist_le_dist_of_mapsTo_ball_self` no longer match their names or docstrings: the hypotheses have been weakened to `closedBall (f c) R`, so these lemmas no longer express the “maps a disk to itself / fixes the center” special case advertised by the `_self` naming. In particular, `dist_le_dist_of_mapsTo_ball_self` now concludes `dist (f z) (f c) ≤ dist z c`, not the documented `dist (f z) c ≤ dist z c`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restore the old special-case assumptions/conclusions (`MapsTo f (ball c R) (closedBall c R)` plus `f c = c`) for the existing names, or rename these generalized lemmas to something like `norm_deriv_le_one_of_mapsTo_ball_same_radius` / `dist_le_dist_of_mapsTo_ball_same_radius` and then reintroduce the old `_self` wrappers as one-line corollaries.

findings.claim: The module header now lists `Complex.abs_deriv_le_div_of_mapsTo_ball` and `Complex.abs_deriv_le_one_of_mapsTo_ball`, but there are no such declarations in the file. The same header and several docstrings also still describe the old self-map statements (`dist (f z) c ≤ dist z c`, `f : ℂ → ℂ`) even though the implemented lemmas were generalized/changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the top-level bullet list and affected docstrings to mention the declarations that actually exist (`norm_deriv_le_div_of_mapsTo_ball`, `norm_deriv_le_one_of_mapsTo_ball`, etc.) and to state the new hypotheses/conclusions accurately; or add the missing `abs_...` aliases if those names are intended to remain part of the API.

findings.claim: `iteratedDeriv_comp_const_sub` duplicates the existing lemma `iteratedDeriv_comp_neg` up to the trivial translation rewrite `fun z ↦ f (s - z) = fun z ↦ (fun y ↦ f (s + y)) (-z)`. Adding both names for the same fact needlessly enlarges the API.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `iteratedDeriv_comp_const_sub`, and when needed derive it from `iteratedDeriv_comp_neg` (or restate/prove it via that lemma in a local proof) instead of introducing a new top-level declaration.

findings.claim: The new `@[fun_prop]` tags do not appear to provide the intended automation for Schwartz functions. In a verification snippet importing this file, `fun_prop` still fails on goals like `ContDiff ℝ n f`, `ContDiffAt ℝ n f x`, `Differentiable ℝ f`, and `DifferentiableAt ℝ f x`, even though `continuity` does succeed for `Continuous f`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either register these lemmas in the form expected by the `fun_prop` machinery for coercions from `𝓢(E, F)` to functions, or drop the ineffective `@[fun_prop]` tags from `smooth`, `contDiffAt`, `continuous`, `differentiable`, and `differentiableAt` until the corresponding `fun_prop` support is actually wired up.

findings.claim: This file explicitly notes that its pointwise section should be kept in sync with `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Submonoid/Pointwise.lean`, but the analogous `Submonoid.closure_pow_le` / `closure_pow` still have the old `n ≠ 0` API. Leaving only the subgroup side updated creates avoidable API drift between the parallel developments.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the corresponding change in `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Submonoid/Pointwise.lean` as well: remove the `n ≠ 0` hypothesis from `Submonoid.closure_pow_le`, add the `n = 0` base case there, and simplify `Submonoid.closure_pow` to use the strengthened lemma.

findings.claim: The new lemma is an awkwardly named reformulation of facts that are already present a few lines later (`card_sdiff_le_card_sdiff_iff`, `card_sdiff_lt_card_sdiff_iff`, `card_sdiff_eq_card_sdiff_iff`). As stated over `ℕ`, `#t - #s = #(t \ s) - #(s \ t)` is less natural and less reusable than the order/equality API already used in this file, so adding it under the name `eq_card_diff_of_sdiff` looks like API clutter rather than a canonical theorem.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop this lemma and keep `le_card_sdiff` proved directly, or replace it with a more canonical/additive statement that avoids truncated subtraction (for example an `+`-form such as `#t + #(s \ t) = #s + #(t \ s)` if that is what downstream users need), together with a name matching the existing `card_sdiff_*` family.
